result.summary: This PR replaces the kernel library's per-connection logging handle (btck_LoggingConnection, with create/destroy functions) with a single global btck_logging_set_callback function, since the underlying LogInstance() and all logging configuration are already process-wide singletons. It introduces a KernelLogger singleton to own the logging connection lifetime, intentionally leaked at process exit to avoid static-destruction-order hazards. The change touches bitcoinkernel.h/.cpp, the C++ wrapper, the bitcoin-chainstate example, and kernel unit tests.
result.problem: The current btck_LoggingConnection API implies that separate logger instances can have independent state, when in fact all kernel logging configuration is global; this misleads kernel library consumers about the semantics they are getting. The author states the fix is meant to make the interface self-explanatory rather than to add capability.

result.card: This PR simplifies the libbitcoinkernel logging API by replacing the per-connection btck_LoggingConnection handle with a single global btck_logging_set_callback function, since kernel logging configuration is already a process-wide singleton and the per-connection handle misleadingly implied independent logger state. It is a kernel-API clarity change with no consensus, performance, or fund-safety stakes; the strongest evidence of importance is the author's claim it will be reused by future logging work in #34374, though that work is described as orthogonal rather than blocked. Two reviewers (sedited, w0xlt) support the direction, but ryanofsky, who is actively developing the competing contextualized-logging approach in #30342/#34374, raised an unresolved design objection that the change could prematurely limit functionality; the author rebutted it once and there has been no further reply. Separately, w0xlt flagged in July that one of the modified tests leaks global logging state into later tests, with a concrete fix suggested, and this has not been implemented in the seven months since; that unresolved, material request pauses productive review of the current diff. No dependency blocks this PR, and it does not itself block other work despite touching a related design area.
